title: Was the Model Given the Right Action? Auditing and Repairing Action Interfaces in Navigation World Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.34739v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: World models are evaluated by predicting future observations from actions. These evaluations assume that actions are prepared the same way as during training, but an unchecked mismatch can make a model appear less accurate than it is. We audit this assumption in Navigation World Models (NWM) and find three interacting differences between its training and rollout code. Correcting the inputs, without retraining, reduces mean visual prediction error by 42%, measured with DreamSim on the RECON navigation dataset. The correction also changes the ranking of NWM checkpoints in an exploratory analysis and removes or reduces two alternative models' measured advantages. Correcting only the normalization offset instead increases error, showing why interacting mismatches must be checked together. translated_title: 模型是否收到了正确的动作？导航世界模型中动作接口的审计与修复
translated_abstract: 世界模型通过从动作预测未来观测来进行评估。这些评估假设动作的准备方式与训练时相同，但未经检查的不匹配可能使模型看起来不如其实际水平准确。我们在导航世界模型（NWM）中审计了这一假设，发现其训练代码与推演代码之间存在三个相互作用的差异。在不重新训练的情况下修正输入，使平均视觉预测误差降低了42%（在RECON导航数据集上使用DreamSim测量）。该修正还在探索性分析中改变了NWM检查点的排名，并消除或减少了两个替代模型所测得的优势。仅修正归一化偏移反而会增加误差，这表明相互作用的失配必须一起检查。为了测试对输入准备的敏感性是否超出NWM的范围，我们故意在两个替代模型中引入编码错误；两者都变得……
tldr: 该论文审计了导航世界模型（NWM）训练与推演代码之间相互作用的动作输入差异，发现无需重新训练、仅修正输入准备方式即可将视觉预测误差降低42%，并改变了模型间的性能排名，证明相互作用的输入失配必须联合检查。
en_tdlr: By auditing interacting mismatches in the action interface between training and rollout code of Navigation World Models, this paper shows that correcting input preparation—without retraining—reduces visual prediction error by 42% and alters model rankings, demonstrating that interacting input mismatches must be checked together.
